THE 2026 ROAD RUNNING SHOE AWARDS

Best Shoes
of the Year

2026 was an incredible year for road running shoes. From dependable daily trainers to innovative marathon racers and unexpected standouts, there was no shortage of great shoes to put miles on.

At 9 to 5 Runners, we all have different running styles, goals, and preferences. What works for one reviewer might not work for another, and that's what makes these awards interesting.

Rather than crown one overall winner, each of our reviewers will select their favorite road running shoe across six categories.

Real runners. Real miles. 100% our own opinions.

Welcome to the 9 to 5 Runners Best of 2026 Road Running Shoe Awards!

Daily TrainerSpeed DayLong Run ShoeRecovery DayRace DaySleeper Shoe of the Year

01 Daily Trainer

CODY’S PICK

Saucony Endorphin Azura

I’ve always wondered what the Endorphin Speed would feel like without a plate, and Saucony finally answered my question. Turns out, you don’t need a plate in everything (shocking, I know). The Azura checked all the boxes for me – comfortable, versatile, and responsive. It’s a shoe that can do a little bit of everything and makes it increasingly difficult to justify the ridiculous number of running shoes I own.

EMILY’S PICK

Topo Specter 3

Perhaps my favorite shoe of the year is also the one I'm most surprised by. If you had told me I'd have a Topo shoe on my "Best Of" list for 2026, I would have told you you're insane. But here we are, and the Topo Specter 3 is my favorite daily trainer of 2026.

Sure, you could also consider this a speed-day shoe, but the Specter 3 is so versatile that I found myself reaching for it on everyday runs. The RevFoam midsole sings at pretty much any pace, providing plenty of responsive cushioning to go the distance, while the geometry rocks you up onto your toes and encourages you to pick up the pace. The upper feels great, and the shoe as a whole is durable. With the exception of its looks, the Topo Specter 3 is pretty much my dream shoe. I found myself reaching for it day after day, and I still am. It absolutely blew me away.

BLAKE’S PICK

ASICS Novablast 6

I feel like the traditional daily trainer category is slowly dying as people's rotations get bigger, and shoes become more versatile, but the Novablast 6 was one shoe I loved using as my workhorse. It was comfortable enough for any type of distance, and the ATPU FF Turbo^2 in the forefoot felt super energetic if I decided I was feeling spicy and wanted to push the pace a little. This is one shoe I kept coming back to when I wanted a reliable, versatile, workhorse.

ERIC’S PICK

ASICS Novablast 6

For a daily pick I want something that feels great for shorts bursts of speed to finish daily miles strong or even with strides. I don't want it to be too heavy or don't need to to be too crazy either. The NovaBlast 6 finds the perfect balance of daily usage with performance elements for a fantastic overall ride

02 Speed Day

CODY’S PICK

Saucony Endorphin Speed 6

The Speed 6 quickly became my go-to shoe during marathon training. Whether I was hitting a 6:15 pace during speed sessions or locking into a 7:00 pace during long-run workouts, everything just felt right. The foam and responsiveness complemented my stride perfectly, making faster efforts feel smooth and natural. It’s one of those shoes that makes me feel a little faster than I actually am – and as a dad runner approaching 40, I’ll take all the help I can get.

EMILY’S PICK

New Balance SuperComp Rebel v1

This was an extremely hard decision. Before the NYC Marathon, I probably would have told you the ASICS Sonicblast 2 was my speed shoe of the year. But after 26.2 grueling miles through the five boroughs, I've got to give it to the New Balance SC Rebel.

I had a few minor issues with the sizing, but otherwise, the midsole of this shoe is fantastic when it comes to picking up the pace. The Infinion foam, paired with the Energy Arc plate in the center, creates an aggressive ride that still manages to keep your feet protected. Some speed-day shoes can leave you feeling banged up at the end of a run, but my legs felt fresh as a daisy after tempo sessions and bounced back relatively quickly after the marathon.

I also really appreciate what New Balance did with the SC Rebel. They took two shoes that were sort of lost in the lineup and combined them to create an absolute banger. Whether you're ripping through workouts or trying to hold marathon pace for 26.2 miles, the New Balance SC Rebel has got you covered.

BLAKE’S PICK

Topo Specter 3

I had never tried Topo before, but my fellow reviewers kept telling me how amazing the Specter 3 was, so I decided to give it a try. Usually wider/more anatomical toe boxes feel too wide and roomy for my narrower foot, however I found the Specter 3 to fit perfectly where my toes could spread out, but weren't swimming. The midsole is the area that blew me away though. It uses RevFoam which is ATPU based, and has a smooth rocker that really rolls you through you stride. It's a versatile shoe, but I particularly enjoyed it for long tempo runs and faster efforts. The ATPU foam was super energetic and I just wanted to go fast. I'd say it challengers the Megablast for a fraction of the cost.

ERIC’S PICK

New Balance SuperComp Rebel v1

Maybe the easiest category for me. The modern speed trainer is somewhat dead in my mind but the SC Rebel V1 manages to provide that extra kick without sacrificing comfort. Interestingly I would take this over the SC Elite v6 at any distance or workout

03 Long Run Shoe

CODY’S PICK

ASICS Superblast 3

I might sound like a broken record at this point, but the Superblast is just soooo good, and the 3 is no exception. I used this shoe throughout two marathon training blocks, and it consistently babied my legs while providing a comfortable, responsive ride. Even on those 18–22-mile long runs, my legs felt surprisingly good. Any shoe that makes running 20 miles seem like a reasonable Sunday morning activity deserves an award.

EMILY’S PICK

ASICS Superblast 3

Don't worry, ASICS lovers. The Sonicblast 2 might have been knocked from the top speed spot, but the Superblast 3 is holding it down in the long-run category. The Superblast is just so consistent, and the 3 is my favorite version yet.

The dual-layer midsole, featuring ASICS' race-day FF Leap foam on top of a base layer of FF Blast Plus, creates a bouncy and energetic underfoot sensation. Long-run shoes have a tendency to feel a bit heavy and dense, but the Superblast 3 is the opposite. It's relatively lightweight despite the massive chunk of foam sitting under your foot.

The upper is also thin but provides a great lockdown onto the platform. I also love the addition of the trampoline pod in the center of the midsole, which gives you just a little more propulsion and responsiveness. The Superblast 3 is like the Energizer Bunny. It could go all day. I'd love to run a marathon in it, and who knows... maybe I will.

BLAKE’S PICK

ASICS Superblast 3

My idea of a perfect long run shoe is something that has lots of protection and comfort, yet can also be versatile enough for easy days and speedier long runs. Superblast 3 checks all these boxes. Plenty of foam underfoot, comfortable, and something that feels soft and bouncy taking it slow, yet is light and energetic enough to pick up the pace. The FF Leap ATPU foam is the same found in ASICS race day lineup and is the key to this shoe's magic. The weight to performance to cushion ratio all lineup in this one.

ERIC’S PICK

Topo Specter 3

This was the hardest category for me to choose. There are quite a few options but I think the Specter 3 is the most versatile of the bunch. Amazing bounce, comfortable fit, all elements you want to lock in and cruise

04 Recovery Day

CODY’S PICK

Salomon Aero Glide 4

The Aero Glide 4 is everything I want in a recovery shoe. It's soft, protective, and comfortable without feeling like I'm running through quicksand. What I really appreciated was how smooth the ride felt, even when my legs were completely trashed from a previous workout. Salomon continues to impress me on the road side, and this became the shoe I reached for when my legs wanted a rest day but my training plan said otherwise.

EMILY’S PICK

Brooks Glycerin Max 3

The Brooks Glycerin Max 3 came in and swept the recovery category at the last second! I thought this shoe was going to be a brick. Slow, heavy, dense, etc. I couldn't have been more wrong.

Much like the ASICS Superblast 3, the Glycerin Max 3 is surprisingly lightweight for a shoe with such an absurdly large midsole. The nitrogen-infused DNA Rise Tuned foam is the perfect mixture of soft and fun. The upper is a bit on the warm side, but I think that comes with the territory when you're dealing with a shoe this large.

The geometry of the Glycerin Max 3 gives runners a surprisingly versatile ride. It works great for slow recovery miles but can also handle your everyday training runs (if you're into all that cushioning). The platform is also nice and wide, which helps with stability and gives your foot even more protection.

I absolutely love the underfoot sensation in the Brooks Glycerin Max 3.

BLAKE’S PICK

ASICS GEL-SLOWCUSH

Typically something like the Clifton or Triumph is what I'd reach for on recovery days, but this year we saw a new category of premium recovery shoes emerge. They might not be the most versatile, but they definitely excel at taking it easy. I found that the FF Luxe+ in the ASICS Gel-Slowcush was squishier than anything in the Blast line, but still had a bit of bounce back to it. If I wanted a shoe that felt cushy, premium, and just absorbed all the shock, the Slowcush was always my choice. Is $200 for a bit of a one-trick pony a lot? Yes. But once you experience the premium recovery cushioning, it's hard to go back.

ERIC’S PICK

ASICS GEL-SLOWCUSH

This shoe may have single handedly changed my opinion on recovery shoes. I have not run in another shoe that was so cushy yet stable and smooth. I have put 30+ miles running but hours upon hours of walking and standing in these because they have been the perfect post long run shoe when the legs are feeling trashed

05 Race Day

CODY’S PICK

Nike Alphafly 4

The Alphafly 4 would have been my Philadelphia Marathon shoe had my body decided to cooperate. I ripped off a 19-mile training run in this shoe, and hitting my target paces felt almost effortless. The updated upper was the biggest selling point for me – the lockdown was spot on, and the midsole geometry worked incredibly well with my stride. Unfortunately, the shoe was ready for race day, even if I wasn't.

EMILY’S PICK

adidas Adizero Adios Pro 5

The Adidas Adios Pro 5 blew me away. Let's cut to the chase: the ENERGYRIM, instead of a traditional plate or ENERGYRODS, is a game-changer.

Plates can start to feel harsh in the later miles, and after running in the Pro 4 at the Boston Marathon, I can attest that the ENERGYRODS felt a little rough as well. The rim technology gives you even more foam under your foot while still providing tons of forward propulsion. The LIGHTSTRIKE PRO foam is insanely good, so the more of it, the better.

The fit is also great, which is especially important in a race-day shoe. There's a nice amount of stretch to the Lightlock 2.0 material, making it pretty accommodating.

This is an A++ update to an already great shoe, and I really wish I had been able to run Boston in it!

BLAKE’S PICK

Nike Alphafly 4

The original Alphafly has always held a spot in my heart for marathon racing, so I might have some bias towards the shoe, but I loved the updates to the Alphafly 4. It's not the most aggressive, or snappiest shoe out there, but it is one of the most comfortable. The roomier upper, softer midsole, and signature Alphafly bounce made for enjoyable workouts and races. I am really curious about the Apex though and if it takes the things I love about the Alphafly, and takes them up a notch.

ERIC’S PICK

Li-Ning Feidian 6 Elite

One of very few shoes that blew me away this year. The foam is transcendent, keeping the legs fresh while still propelling you forward. My only knock is it can be a little unstable but it's currently my choice the next time I line up on a flat marathon course

06 Sleeper Shoe of the Year

CODY’S PICK

Craft Atmosfär 1

This shoe, in my opinion, defies all logic. With a stack height of over 50mm, it has no business being this stable, responsive, or fast – yet somehow, Craft pulled it off. Craft isn't necessarily known for its road running shoes, but the Atmosfär 1 quickly became a shoe I found myself recommending to everyone. If you had told me at the beginning of the year that one of my favorite road shoes would come from Craft, I probably would have laughed. Well, here we are.

EMILY’S PICK

RAD UFO

It's technically a 2025 shoe, but most of my miles in the RAD UFO came in 2026. I bought this shoe based on looks alone. I thought it was absolutely insane-looking, with its bright pink colorway and almost alien-like silhouette. Turns out, the underfoot feel is just as wild.

The theme of this year continues: it's another shoe that's extremely lightweight for the amount of cushioning it provides. The rocker allows the PEBA-based SUPEFOAM to respond well at tempo paces, but it can also double as your easy-day trainer.

I've run this shoe into the ground, and it's still going strong after well over 100 miles. If it were a 2026 release, this would have been a serious contender for my favorite shoe of the year.

It just goes to show that some of the best shoes can come from brands you least expect.

BLAKE’S PICK

TYR Valkyrie Elite 2

One brand that has been dropping some great shoes that I think fly under the radar are TYR. The Maverick was one of my favorite shoes last year, and this year the Valkyrie Elite 2 combines the aggressiveness of the Fast-R 3 and the bouncy foam of the Metaspeed Ray, to produce a fun, fast, and snappy racier.

ERIC’S PICK

361° Mega 3 Pro

361 has quietly released some really solid shoes but the Mega 3 Pro is sneaking up on special territory. This is a late entry and I don't even have my full review miles on it yet which is why I can't let it fully take a category. This is as close as you can get to a do it all shoe and dare I say, it improves on the EVO SL and Xiaonian formula that so many love
